arrival.speaker: halden
arrival.text: Morning, you two. Mind that sack by the door.

arrival.speaker: halden
arrival.text: Ah. Thank you. I meant to go and fetch it.

arrival.speaker: tomas
arrival.text: She said your hands were hurting.

arrival.speaker: halden
arrival.text: They are. Particularly when people keep asking me to tell them about it.

arrival.speaker: halden
arrival.text: It would. I need the doorway clear before I bring any more flour through.

arrival.speaker: halden
arrival.text: On the dry pallet by the north wall. Three sacks. Keep them off the floor.

arrival.speaker: caelan
arrival.text: There’s more waiting at the mill?

arrival.speaker: halden
arrival.text: More grain to grind, yes. Everyone wants to bake before the Festival of Light. I’d like to give them time to do it.

arrival.speaker: tomas
arrival.text: I can carry it. Just help me get it settled.

arrival.speaker: caelan
arrival.text: All right. We’ll lift it together.

arrival.speaker: halden
arrival.text: Keep it close once you’ve got it. And put it down if you need to. There’s no prize for getting there without stopping.

reminder.speaker: halden
reminder.text: Those three sacks by the door, onto the dry pallet by the north wall. Take your time.

reminder.speaker: tomas
reminder.text: I’m ready for the middle one when you are.

conclusion.speaker: halden
conclusion.text: That’s much better. I can get through here again.

conclusion.speaker: caelan
conclusion.text: You’ve still got a lot to do.

conclusion.speaker: halden
conclusion.text: I have. But I can manage the mill without carrying everything in and out as well.

conclusion.speaker: caelan
conclusion.text: We can tell Serene you need another pair of hands.

conclusion.speaker: halden
conclusion.text: For the carrying, perhaps. Tell her I asked, before she decides I need someone watching me all day.

conclusion.speaker: halden
conclusion.text: And thank you. Both of you.

conclusion.speaker: halden
conclusion.text: The wheel’s been making an awkward noise, too. I’ll have to look at it.

conclusion.speaker: tomas
conclusion.text: Would Mira know what it is?

conclusion.speaker: halden
conclusion.text: She might. She learned her way around that mill working with me. These days she notices things I’ve walked past twice.

conclusion.speaker: halden
conclusion.text: Not yet. She’s got people coming to her workshop with their own repairs.

conclusion.speaker: caelan
conclusion.text: She’d probably rather hear about it before something breaks.

conclusion.speaker: halden
conclusion.text: *rubs his hand* Yes. I suppose she would.

goodbye.speaker: tomas
goodbye.text: I’d better get back. Mother will be waiting to move the tables.

goodbye.speaker: caelan
goodbye.text: I’ve still got Elira by the southern bridge and the Venns on the eastern terrace.

goodbye.speaker: tomas
goodbye.text: You don’t have to hurry back for us.

goodbye.speaker: tomas
goodbye.text: You were about to tell me to wait for you.

goodbye.speaker: caelan
goodbye.text: *after a pause* I was going to say I’d help when I got back.

goodbye.speaker: tomas
goodbye.text: We’ll leave you something if there’s anything left.
